description: Minimal Nim object model: a CatchableError-rooted error hierarchy, a RootObj-rooted repository pair, and a variant object. Exercises type/proc extraction, type->method CONTAINS, and — the reason the fixture exists (#6370) — `= ref object of Base` inheritance, including the three other things Nim spells `of` which must NOT produce an edge.

expected_entities.name: Config
expected_entities.note: Plain object, no `of` clause — the negative half of the entity set.

expected_entities.name: Node
expected_entities.note: Inherits RootObj AND carries a case-variant section whose branches are also `of`.

expected_entities.name: describe
expected_entities.note: Same name as errors.nim's describe; source_file keeps them apart.

expected_entities.name: Payload
expected_entities.note: Variant object with NO base — the type that distinguishes an anchored read from a forward search.

expected_entities.name: Cursor
expected_entities.note: Base-less object sitting immediately above a runtime type test.

expected_entities.name: store.nim
expected_entities.note: #6815: the #577 file carrier. store.nim is the ONE file in this fixture with an `import` line (`import tables, strutils`), and buildImportEntities anchors both IMPORTS edges on the path, so this is the entity that gives them a real FROM end. Paired with the forbidden_entities rows below for the over-firing direction.

expected_relationships.note: #6370: `AppError* = ref object of CatchableError`. CatchableError is in Nim's stdlib, outside the tree, so a bare-name target is correct.

#6370: base declared in the SAME file, so this row also grades that the edge is anchored on the TYPE and not on the file — were all three types in errors.nim merged onto one file node, from_file narrowing could not tell them apart.
#6370: the second leaf on the same base — two types sharing one parent.
#6370: `ref object of RootObj`, Nim's universal object root.
#6370: a second in-file base, in a different file from the errors hierarchy, so a predicate hard-coded to either file or to CatchableError/AppError fails here.

#6370: Node inherits RootObj AND has a case-variant section. The forbidden rows below assert the variant branches did not also become edges, so this row and those rows together grade both directions on ONE declaration.
#6370: `Span* = object of RootObj` — the NON-ref form. Every other inheriting type in this fixture is `ref object of`, so this is the only row that fails when a producer handles `ref object` alone.
Pre-existing nim behaviour: a proc whose parameter list names the type is CONTAINed by it. Held here so the fixture measures more than the one edge kind #6370 adds.

forbidden_relationships.note: #6370 OVER-FIRING, object variant: `of nkInt:` is a variant branch inside Node's body. NOT FIRED by any single-edit mutant tried — Node's FIRST `of` is its real base, so removing the anchor still gets Node right. Kept as an absence fence for a whole-declaration or whole-file regex producer, which is the shape the graphql YAML rule pack has (it emits an edge for a commented-out type). The row that actually fires under the anchor mutant is Payload -> nkInt below.
#6370 OVER-FIRING, object variant: Node's second variant branch. Same grading status as the row above — an absence fence, not a mutant-killed row.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, runtime type test: `x of Node` in atNode() is a TYPE TEST, not a declaration. Cursor is base-less and declared immediately above atNode, so a forward search from Cursor lands on it. Deliberately targets Node rather than Cursor: a self-target would be blocked by the self-edge guard as well as by the anchor, and a row that needs TWO mutants to fire grades neither.
#6370 OVER-FIRING: Config is a plain `object` with no clause. Nim gives every object an implicit root, but nothing in the SOURCE says RootObj, and this extractor must report what is written.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, enum: `of` is not part of the enum grammar, so NodeKind must never acquire a base. FIRES, verified: with BOTH the anchor and the kind restriction removed, NodeKind binds `RootObj` — the first `of` after `enum` is Node's inheritance clause three lines further down, not `of nkInt`. The row originally named nkInt and was therefore unfireable; naming what the compound mutant actually produces is what makes it graded. The kind restriction on its own is killed at the unit level by TestNimHierarchy_NonObjectKindsNeverExtend.

#6370 OVER-FIRING: Payload has NO base and its first `of` is a variant branch. Node cannot catch this — Node's first `of` IS its base, so a producer that scans the whole declaration rather than anchoring at the `object` keyword still gets Node right. This row and the next are the two the unanchored mutant fails.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, object variant: Payload's second variant branch. The FIRST branch (nkInt) is the one the anchor mutant trips; this row additionally fences a producer that emits EVERY `of` in a declaration rather than the first.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, comment: `of PhantomBase` sits in a `#` comment inside Config's body. This extractor has no comment awareness — the anchor is the only reason it does not fire — and a YAML rule pack producer WOULD fire, which is exactly what the graphql pack does for a commented-out SDL type. This is the row a plain forward search trips first.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, case statement: `of httpPort:` is a branch of scheme()'s `case`, in a different declaration entirely. Config is the last type in store.nim, so a forward search that DID scrub comments trips this one instead — the two Config rows grade two different mutants, not one twice.

forbidden_entities.name: Ghost
forbidden_entities.note: #6370: `# type Ghost = ref object of Widget` is COMMENTED OUT in errors.nim. NOT REACHABLE by any mutant of this extractor, stated plainly rather than implied: typeRE is anchored `(?m)^[ \t]*(?:type\s+)?[A-Z]`, so a `#` before `type` makes the line structurally unmatchable and no loosening of the `of` clause can reach it. Kept as an absence fence for a rule-pack producer — internal/engine/rules/graphql/frameworks/graphql_schema.yaml does exactly this for a commented-out SDL type — and nim has no rule pack today. The reachable version of this hazard IS a real defect and is pinned instead as TestNimHierarchy_InsideTripleQuotedStringOverFires_KnownDivergence: the same declaration inside a """…""" block IS extracted, entity and EXTENDS edge alike. It is deliberately not in this fixture, because a golden fixture must stay green.

forbidden_entities.name: Widget
forbidden_entities.note: #6370: the base named in that same commented-out line. Same grading status as the row above — an unreachable fence, not a mutant-killed row.

forbidden_entities.name: errors.nim
forbidden_entities.note: #6815 OVER-FIRING control. errors.nim has no import, include or from-import, so it anchors no edge on its path and must mint no file carrier. This row is REACHABLE by a mutant, unlike the two above: making extractor.PrependFileCarrier unconditional turns it red immediately. Recall cannot see that mutant — the store.nim carrier row stays green whether the carrier is minted for one file or for every file.

forbidden_entities.name: model.nim
forbidden_entities.note: #6815 OVER-FIRING control, second file. Held so the check is graded on more than one negative: a predicate hard-coded to exempt errors.nim would satisfy the row above and fail this one.
